chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said:

I had a slave-girl with whom I was greatly taken, so I wrote seeking instruction regarding having a child from her. Then there came the reply: “Have a child from her, and Allah does whatever He wills.” So I had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant; then she miscarried, and died.

key_terms.جَارِيَةٌ: a female slave-girl owned by the speaker
key_terms.فَوَطِئْتُهَا: so I had intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about seeking instruction on istīlād of a slave-girl and Allah’s will in the outcome?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a man’s consultation regarding istīlād of his slave-girl and the reply permitting it while affirming that Allah does whatever He wills. The report also relates the subsequent events of pregnancy, miscarriage, and her death, reflecting both a legal context and recognition of divine decree.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Salih who said,

‘There was a maid of mine whom I was fascinated with, and I wrote for the orders with regards to procreating with her. So there arrived (a letter from the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>): ‘Procreate with her and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Does whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to’. So I copulated with her and she became pregnant, then she miscarried and she died’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salih who has said the following.

“I had a female slave that had attracted my attention. I wrote to him (Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) requesting permission to have a child from her. The answer came, “You may do so but Allah does whatever He wants.” I went to bed with her and she became pregnant. The fetus fell off prematurely and she died.”
